result.title: Uneven gains in protein-RNA affinity and mutation-effect prediction
result.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Supplementary material included as an ancillary file
result.summary: Accurate matched affinities determine mutation effects, but gains in aggregate affinity prediction may transfer unevenly to average effects, ordering and local accuracy. We evaluated eleven method families using method-specific matched populations. Controlled CoPRA reduced absolute-affinity mean absolute error from 1.2898 to 1.1431 pKd. Across 220 mutation pairs from 20 families, it generated stronger responses and improved mean-effect accuracy, with uncertain ranking gains and no decrease in mean centered local error. In an independent external test (24 quantitative pairs from three source-matched families), absolute and ordinary mutation-effect errors fell in all three families. Mean centered local error fell from 0.4198 to 0.3761 pKd, with improvements in two families and higher error in one. Error decomposition localized gains in landscape means. PRA-Pred feature tracing, fixed-weight M2-PRNet input controls and matched supervision interventions identified specific restrictions on mutation response. These results establish the need to evaluate average effects, ordering and quantitative local variation jointly.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 protein-RNA 亲和力与突变效应预测上评估十一种方法族，检验聚合亲和力预测的提升是否能均匀转移到平均效应、排序与局部定量精度，并用误差分解、特征追踪与匹配监督干预定位突变响应受限之处。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将总误差分解为均值效应、排序与中心化局部误差，并配合匹配种群与监督干预的做法，可能为 LVR 中「聚合收益是否转移到局部 latent 推理」的评价设计及贡献分配提供参照，可迁移性需核查。
